## Verdict: REJECT (one Important test-coverage gap at the important threshold)

This PR is not ready to merge: it deletes the only tests that show the read-only guard refuses a `MERGE` hidden inside a common table expression, and it does not replace them with MySQL versions.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `tests/unit/test_safety.py` (the CTE-nested write group of `_BYPASS_CORPUS`, around lines 222-238) no longer has any entry that puts a `MERGE` inside a common table expression. The base had four such entries (base lines 216-231, for example `WITH changed AS (MERGE INTO target t USING source s ON t.id=s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE RETURNING t.id) SELECT * FROM changed`). They used dialect `postgres` and were deleted rather than moved to `mysql`, while their `INSERT`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE` neighbours were moved. The only remaining `MERGE` case is the root-level statement at line 55, which the root-type check refuses before the nested-write walk runs. So the `exp.Merge` entry in the nested-write type list (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:377`) has no test of its own, and removing it would not fail any test. Whether sqlglot parses this statement under `mysql` or with no dialect was not checked. (raised by 1/6 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (7)

<details><summary>7 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 109-116: the new `DatabaseConfig.url` validator accepts only `mysql`, `mysql+<driver>` or `sqlite…` schemes, but the code that acts on the URL still accepts any scheme that starts with `mysql`. That looser check is in `build_sql_runner` (`src/sqllens/agent/factory.py:250`), `probe_database` (`src/sqllens/preflight.py:115`) and `sqlglot_dialect_for_url` (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:187`). A `Config` built without validation (for example with `model_construct`) or a direct call with `mysqlx://…` gets a `MySQLRunner` or a pymysql connect attempt, not the unsupported-scheme refusal. Normal config loading refuses it correctly. The `DatabaseConfig.dialect` property also does not lowercase the scheme, but its only consumer lowercases it. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 111-116: the same scheme mismatch, seen as an error-handling risk. A programmatic caller that skips config validation and passes `mysqlx://` reaches `MySQLRunner` / `pymysql.connect` and fails later with a driver error, not the structured unsupported-scheme error. No CLI path reaches it, and `docs/internal/agent/factory.md` and `docs/internal/setup/preflight.md` describe the gap accurately. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `tests/unit/test_safety.py` lines 1175-1185, `test_call_after_nested_comment_markers_is_checked`: the row changed from `postgres` to `("mysql", "sleep(0)", "Nested MySQL comments")`. Under `mysql` the nested-comment check refuses the input before any function is looked at. So this row does not show that a call after nested comment markers is checked, as the test name says, and it repeats the nested-comment refusals already pinned at lines 1125 and 1158. Only the `sqlite` row still reaches the function denylist. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `tests/unit/test_safety_whole_row.py` line 176: the added comment `# sqlite_ is a catalog prefix only on sqlite.` is broader than the code. With no dialect, or a dialect that has no catalog entry, every prefix counts, `sqlite_` included. The comment at line 162 of the same file says exactly that, so the two comments disagree. - VC-38: FAIL (suggestion) — The SqlRunner.run_sql docstring says require_base_tables makes implementations refuse views, unverified relation kinds, calls whose names match database-defined routines, and failed catalog lookups before running SQL. [src/sqllens/agent/capabilities/sql_runner/base.py:30]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The docstring at src/sqllens/agent/capabilities/sql_runner/base.py:30-34 does say require_base_tables makes implementations refuse views, unverified relation kinds, calls matching database-defined routines and failed catalog lookups. Checked against verify_base_tables (src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:98-138) and its helpers. Matches: (1) unverified kinds are refused (relations.py:185-188); (2) a lookup that raises is turned into RlsError (125-138); (3) views are refused (181-184); (4) under mysql a call name matching an information_schema.ROUTINES FUNCTION is refused (191-211). Mismatches in the unqualified wording: (a) views are not refused when the relation is one of the nine MySQL information_schema metadata views in _METADATA_VIEWS (relations.py:25-32, skipped by `continue` at 162-165). So `SELECT ... FROM information_schema.tables` passes under require_base_tables even though that is a SYSTEM VIEW. This exemption is documented in verify_base_tables' own docstring (103-105) but not in the base-class contract. (b) The routine check runs only for dialect == 'mysql' (relations.py:112); SQLite runs no call check, and the sqlite runner's own docstring (sqlite/sql_runner.py:149-150) names only views and failed lookups. The abstract contract therefore overstates what every implementation does. The item's source is source_authored, so a counterexample in the authored text suffices; the metadata-view input is producible by any MySQL RLS query. Impact is wording only, since the code behavior is intentional and documented elsewhere.

  </details>

- VC-54: FAIL (suggestion) — The docstring asserts probe_database does not run a query against MySQL, only opens and closes a pymysql connection with a bounded connect timeout. [src/sqllens/preflight.py:90]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  probe_database (src/sqllens/preflight.py:135-149) calls pymysql.connect(host, port, user, password, database, connect_timeout) with no init_command, sql_mode or autocommit, then closes via contextlib.closing. Installed PyMySQL 1.2.4 (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pymysql-1.2.4.dist-info) Connection.connect() unconditionally runs self.set_character_set(self.charset, self.collation) at connections.py:727; set_character_set (653-667) does self._execute_command(COMMAND.COM_QUERY, 'SET NAMES <charset>') and reads the reply. charset defaults to DEFAULT_CHARSET (line 333), so this always fires. sql_mode/init_command/autocommit statements (729-740) are skipped for the probe's arguments, and close() (427-) only sends COM_QUIT. So the probe does issue one COM_QUERY (SET NAMES) round-trip at connect; the docstring's 'Does not run a query against MySQL' (preflight.py:90) is literally inaccurate. Mitigating: it is a session-level SET NAMES needing no table permissions, so the docstring's rationale about permission checks still holds in practice, and the connect timeout bound (line 146) is accurate. Hence a minor docstring inaccuracy.

  </details>

</details>
